book.title: Hoca Ahmed Yesevî and His Student Süleyman the Wise (Hakîm Ata)

pages.title: Who Was Ahmed Yesevî?
pages.content: Ahmed Yesevî was the first great Sufi poet to write in Turkish. His poems are called ‘hikmet’ (wisdom). Sufis try to be very close to Allah. They live a simple life and remember Allah all the time. They learn from a wise teacher how to behave well. Ahmed Yesevî was also a wise teacher and started the Yesevî Sufi School. His school wanted to teach Islam and Sufism to the Turkish people. He is also called Pîr-i Turkistan. The Persian word ‘pîr’ means an elder or a guide. This guide helps people to be good people in this life and find peace after death. He was a very important teacher in Turkish Islamic culture.

vocabulary.definition: A poet who writes about being close to Allah.
Act in a good and polite way.
A person who shows others the right way.

pages.title: Childhood and Teachers
pages.content:
Historians say that he was born in East Turkestan in the second half of the 11th century. When he was young, he moved to the city of Yesi in Turkestan. Today, the city of Yesi is in Kazakhstan. Ahmed Yesevî studied with Arslan Baba, a wise teacher, and got a good education. He grew up in Turkestan. At that time, Turkestan was a center for education and science. He lived during the Karakhanid period (840–1212).

Some time after Arslan Baba’s death, he traveled to Bukhara. Today, Bukhara is a famous city in Uzbekistan. It was one of the important Islamic centers at that time. There, he learned from great teachers and Sufi masters. They guided him in the Sufi way. After his masters died, he stayed in that region for some time. Then, he returned to Yesi and guided people there until he died in 1166.

pages.title: What Is Wisdom?
pages.content:
Wisdom helps us understand the reason and purpose of our actions. Without it, rules and duties are just empty tasks.

Law and rules answer the questions ‘What?’ and ‘How?’, but wisdom answers the question ‘Why?’ Knowing our tasks and how to do them is important. But ‘Why should I do it?’ is the most important question.

Our actions only have a real meaning when we know the purpose. All rules and duties are really important because of wisdom.

vocabulary.definition: Why something happens or is done.

pages.title: The Child Who Respected the Qur’an
pages.content:
Turkic people in many places, from Anatolia to the Balkans, deeply love Ahmed Yesevî. Today, there are many beautiful stories about his life.

Here’s one example:

According to a famous story, one day Ahmed Yesevî was sitting in front of his school. He saw a group of children walking by. They were going to the mosque to study the Qur’an. Most of them were carrying their Qur’ans in bags on their shoulders. However, one child was carrying the Qur’an on top of his head to show great respect. Ahmed Yesevî watched this with a warm smile.

When the same child was coming back from class, he walked backwards. He did not want to turn his back on his teacher. Ahmed Yesevî saw this and understood the beautiful meaning in the child’s behavior. He told the boy, “My son! Ask your parents for permission and come to my lessons.” The child got permission from his family and came to Yesevî’s school. For many years, he studied there. He was a very good student and became closer to Allah. This kid’s name was Süleyman.

vocabulary.definition: Stand with his back toward someone.
When someone says you can do something.
Came nearer; made a stronger connection.

pages.title: Wood in the Rain
pages.content: One day, Ahmed Yesevî sent Süleyman and his friends to get wood from the fields. The school needed this wood to cook food for the dervishes, students, and guests. On their way back, it started to rain. Süleyman knew that they needed dry wood to cook the food, so he wanted to keep it dry. He took off his coat and wrapped it around his wood. When the children came back to the school, all the other wood was wet and did not burn. However, Süleyman’s wood was dry and burned easily. Ahmed Yesevî saw the boy’s great respect and love for his duty. He told him, “My son! You did this with a wise heart. From now on, your name is Hakîm Süleyman (Süleyman the Wise).”

vocabulary.definition: Covered something by putting something around it.

pages.title: Hakîm Ata of Khwarazm
pages.content: Süleyman learned many lessons from his teacher and grew up under his guidance. Later, people knew him by the name Hakîm Ata. After finishing his Sufi education, Hakîm Ata left the Yesi region and moved to Khwarazm. Today, this place is in Uzbekistan and Turkmenistan. There, he taught and guided people. Just like his master Ahmed Yesevî, Hakîm Ata also wrote poems in Turkish.

pages.title: Words of Hakîm Ata
pages.content: Hakîm Ata is not as famous as his teacher Ahmed Yesevî. But he is one of the first people to teach Islam and good manners to the Turks. When Turks first became Muslim, he helped them with his wise words. People know him for his famous words: “See every visitor as Khizr and see every night as Laylat al-Qadr.” (Her geleni Hızır, her geceyi Kadir bil). He also has beautiful words about being humble: “Others are wheat, we are chaff; others are good, we are bad.” (Başkası buğday biz saman, başkası yahşi biz yaman).

pages.title: Master Glossary
pages.content: Review all key vocabulary from the book in one place.

vocabulary.definition: A poet who writes about being close to Allah.
vocabulary.storyExample: Ahmed Yesevî was the first great Sufi poet to write in Turkish.
Sufis try to be very close to Allah.

vocabulary.definition: Act in a good and polite way.
vocabulary.storyExample: They learn from a wise teacher how to behave well.

vocabulary.definition: A person who shows others the right way.
vocabulary.storyExample: The Persian word ‘pîr’ means an elder or a guide.
This guide helps people to be good people in this life and find peace after death.

vocabulary.definition: Why something happens or is done.
vocabulary.storyExample: Wisdom helps us understand the reason and purpose of our actions.
Wisdom helps us understand the reason and purpose of our actions.
Without it, rules and duties are just empty tasks.
Without it, rules and duties are just empty tasks.

vocabulary.chapterTitle: The Child Who Respected the Qur’an
vocabulary.storyExample: Ahmed Yesevî watched this with a warm smile.

vocabulary.definition: Stand with his back toward someone.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: The Child Who Respected the Qur’an
vocabulary.storyExample: He did not want to turn his back on his teacher.

vocabulary.definition: When someone says you can do something.
vocabulary.chapterTitle: The Child Who Respected the Qur’an

vocabulary.definition: Came nearer; made a stronger connection.

Ahmed Yesevî saw the boy’s great respect and love for his duty.

pages.title: Language Review
pages.content: Review and use the language of the whole book.

exercises.title: Look: Teacher or Student?
exercises.instructions: Sort the sentences into two groups.
exercises.question: Is it about Ahmed Yesevî or about Süleyman?

items: He started the Yesevî Sufi School.
He carried the Qur’an on his head.

Ahmed Yesevî: He started the Yesevî Sufi School.
Süleyman (Hakîm Ata): He carried the Qur’an on his head.

exercises.explanation: The book tells the story of a teacher (Chapters 1–4) and his student (Chapters 5–8).

feedback.correct: Good. You sorted the teacher and the student.
feedback.incorrect: Is the sentence about the teacher or the student?

exercises.title: Look: Past Forms
exercises.instructions: Choose the sentence with a correct past form.
exercises.question: Which sentence is correct?
exercises.explanation: “Take” is an irregular verb. Its past form is “took”.

feedback.incorrect: What is the past of take?

exercises.title: Look: Was + -ing
exercises.instructions: Is the sentence true or false?
exercises.question: In “One child was carrying the Qur’an on his head”, was carrying shows an action in progress.
exercises.explanation: The past continuous (was / were + -ing) shows an action in progress in the past.

feedback.incorrect: Was the action in progress?

exercises.title: Practise: Linking Words
exercises.instructions: Fill each gap from the word bank. Two words are not needed.
exercises.question: Which word fits?
exercises.fillBlanksText: People loved Yesevî [blank] he used simple language. It started to rain, [blank] Süleyman wrapped his coat around his wood. The other wood was wet. [blank], his wood was dry.
exercises.explanation: “Because” gives a reason. “So” gives a result. “However” shows something different.

feedback.incorrect: Is it a reason, a result or something different?

exercises.title: Practise: Choose the Form
exercises.instructions: Choose the correct form for each sentence.
exercises.question: Which form fits?

formChoices.sentence: His poems are [choice] ‘hikmet’.
[choice] he was young, he moved to Yesi.
Hakîm Ata is not as famous [choice] his teacher.

exercises.explanation: Use “are called” for a name, “when” for a time, and “not as … as” to compare.

feedback.incorrect: Check the name, the time and the comparison.

exercises.title: Practise: Correct the Sentences
exercises.instructions: Find the mistake and choose the correct form.
exercises.question: Which form is correct?

errorItems.sentence: The children was going to the mosque.
After finish his education, he moved to Khwarazm.
The word ‘pîr’ mean an elder or a guide.

exercises.explanation: Use “were” with plural subjects, “-ing” after “after”, and “means” with one word.

feedback.incorrect: Check the verb forms.

exercises.title: Use: A New Context
exercises.instructions: Read about a school today. Fill each gap from the word bank.
exercises.question: Can you use the book’s words in a new text?
exercises.fillBlanksText: In our school, Mr. Demir is a wise [blank]. He always explains the [blank] of our homework. We ask for [blank] before we leave the classroom. Every student has a small [blank] in the classroom.
exercises.explanation: Guide, purpose, permission and duty come from the book. Here they describe a school today.

feedback.correct: Well done. You used the book’s words in a new text.
feedback.incorrect: Read the words around each gap.

exercises.title: Use: Check a Short Text
exercises.instructions: A student wrote about a guest. Find each mistake.
exercises.question: What should the student change?

errorItems.sentence: Yesterday, a guest come to our house.
My mother was cook when the guest arrived.
We was very happy to see him.

exercises.explanation: Use a past verb with yesterday, “was + -ing” for an action in progress, and “were” with we.

feedback.incorrect: Check the verb forms.

exercises.title: Use: A Wise Person I Know
exercises.instructions: Write four to five sentences about a wise person you know.
exercises.question: What does this person do or say?
exercises.explanation: Example: “A wise person I know is my grandmother. She always asks ‘Why?’ before she decides something. One day, I was angry with my friend. She told me to listen to him first. I learned to be patient because she showed me the reason.”

feedback.correct: Check: who the person is, an example and because.

discussionPrompts.question: Say who the person is.
discussionPrompts.example: A wise person I know is …

discussionPrompts.question: Give one example of their wisdom.
Say what you learned, with because.
